items.title: Topic Two's Summary Closes: Karma's Own Timing, and Why the Deva Needed the Buddha

items.zh: 若於先世不作福者，今雖用功，於所樂欲不能果遂。或惟今世造作福者，即於此時，其所樂欲亦不諧偶。由此因緣，後方成辦，所以諸欲名曰待時。
items.en: If one performed no merit in a former life, then however much effort one now applies, one's desired object still fails to be realised. Or, if one performs merit only in this present life, the desired object still does not come together at this very time. Because of this, its accomplishment must wait for a later time — this is why desires are said to "require their proper time."

items.zh: 第四頌中，顯示見斷煩惱斷故，即於現在證初沙門及沙門果；又修所斷煩惱斷故，即於現在證後沙門及沙門果。斷貪愛故，斷我慢故，如是顯示現所證法。又離著故，煙寂靜故，顯示永離熾燃、乃至智者自內所證。彼得如是內所證法，云何令他當得了知？由無燒惱、無所悕望相所表故。
此中前三頌，顯示世尊為諸天說，苾芻不能顯揚如來聖教大義，而我獨能。說是語時，彼既領悟，於苾芻所生陵蔑心及於自身心生憍慢皆得除滅。第四頌中，廣顯如來聖教大義。
items.en: Here, the first three verses show the Blessed One speaking directly to the deity: the monk himself could not unfold the great meaning of the Tathāgata's teaching — only I can. Upon hearing this, the deity awakened to understanding, and both the contempt felt towards the monk and the pride felt in themselves were entirely dispelled. The fourth verse broadly discloses the great meaning of the Tathāgata's teaching itself.

items.title: Topic Three Opens: A Burning Mind, and the Buddha's Fourfold Remedy

items.zh: 欲貪所摧蔽，我心遍燒然。惟大仙哀愍，為說令寂靜。
items.en: Crushed and obscured by craving-desire, my mind is entirely ablaze; great sage, have compassion — teach me how to make it still.

items.zh: 由汝想顛倒，令心遍燒燃；是故常遠離引貪淨妙相。汝當修不淨，常定於一境；為貪火速滅，數數應澆灌。觀非妙諸行，為苦，為無我；亦繫念於身，多修習厭離。修習於無相，壞慢及隨眠。由於慢現觀，當證苦邊際。
items.en: It is your own distorted perception that sets your mind entirely ablaze; therefore always keep far from the alluring, seemingly pure appearance that provokes craving. You should cultivate meditation on impurity, keeping the mind constantly fixed on a single object; to quickly extinguish craving's fire, you should pour water on it again and again. Observe conditioned things — not beautiful, but suffering, but without self; keep mindfulness fixed on the body as well, and cultivate revulsion extensively. Cultivate the signless, and destroy pride along with its latent tendency; through direct realisation concerning pride, you shall reach the very limit of suffering.

items.zh: 云何想顛倒？謂於不淨境，捨不淨相；不正思惟，取淨妙相及取隨好。云何遠離引貪淨相？謂如有一，見少盛色應可愛樂諸母邑已，便攝諸根而不隨念。
items.en: What is distorted perception? It means, regarding an impure object, discarding its impure mark; through improper reflection, taking up instead a seemingly pure, alluring mark, along with its attractive particulars. What is meant by keeping far from the alluring mark that provokes craving? It refers to one who, having seen a young woman in the bloom of youth, lovely and desirable, at once withdraws the senses and does not dwell on what was seen.

items.zh: 云何常定一境修習不淨？

items.title: Meditation on Impurity: The Corpse Outside, the Body Within

items.zh: 謂如有一，先以巧便取於賢善三摩地相，所謂青瘀乃至白骨，或骨瑣相。即以此相，於現所得可愛境界，繫念思惟；如前所取，後亦如是。
items.en: It refers to one who first skilfully grasps the mark belonging to wholesome concentration — the mark of a corpse turning livid, and on through to bare bones, or a scattered skeleton. Taking up this same mark, one fixes mindfulness upon it in reflecting on whatever presently appears as an attractive object; just as one grasped it before, so one continues to grasp it afterwards.

items.zh: 又於內身或自、或他，觀察種種不淨充滿。謂此身中有髮有爪、乃至便利種種不淨。
items.en: And, regarding the body within — one's own or another's — one observes it as filled with impurity of every kind: within this body there is hair, there are nails, and on through to excrement and every other kind of impurity.

items.zh: 云何觀察非妙諸行以之為苦？

items.title: Observing Suffering and Non-Self, and Sustained Practice for the Strongly Afflicted

items.zh: 謂如有一，作是思惟：見少盛色應可愛樂諸母邑已，所生貪愛受用悕望，即是集諦，為眾苦因。由此故生，生已老死，愁歎憂苦種種擾惱從此而生。
items.en: It refers to one who reflects thus: the craving, indulgence, and longing that arise upon seeing a young woman in the bloom of youth, lovely and desirable — this itself is the truth of origination, the cause of every kind of suffering. From this, birth arises; having been born, ageing and death follow, and sorrow, lamentation, grief, and every kind of affliction arise from this in turn.

items.zh: 云何觀察非妙諸行以為無我？
謂如有一，作是思惟：於我身形、女身形中，都無有我及有情等，誰能受用，誰所受用；唯是諸行，唯是諸法，從眾緣生。
items.en: It refers to one who reflects thus: within my own bodily form, or a woman's bodily form, there exists no self and no being of any kind — who, then, could be the one enjoying, and who the one enjoyed? There is only what is conditioned, only these phenomena, arising from a coming-together of many causes.

items.zh: 云何繫念於身多修厭離？
謂如有一，性是猛盛欲貪種類。由是猛盛欲貪類故，雖攝諸根，然被貪欲損壞其心；雖復作意思惟不淨、苦及無我，亦為欲貪損壞其心。由此因緣，彼依不淨、或苦、無我作意思惟，權時厭毀、違逆、不順，於身念住繫念在前，親近、修習、若多修習。彼由多住如是行故，便能斷此猛盛欲貪。
items.en: It refers to one whose disposition belongs to the fiercely intense type of craving-desire. Because their craving is so intensely strong, even withdrawing the senses still leaves the mind damaged by desire; even applying the mind to impurity, suffering, and non-self, the mind is still damaged by desire. For this reason, relying on these same reflections on impurity, suffering, and non-self, one must, for the time being, reject what has already arisen, resist what is now arising, and refuse what is about to arise... drawing near to this practice, cultivating it, and cultivating it extensively. Only by dwelling in such practice at length is one able to sever this fiercely intense craving-desire.

items.zh: 若攝諸根，不為欲貪損壞其心；若復作意思惟不淨、苦及無我，亦不貪欲損壞其心。彼由修習如是行故，諸欲貪纏但現行斷，非隨眠斷。又此欲貪纏及隨眠，略於二種補特伽羅相續可得。一、於異生相續可得，二、於有學相續可得。雖有一分有學身中亦不可得，然於下貪由永斷故，已得安隱；上貪未斷，不得安隱。無學身中，中界、妙界所有貪欲尚不可得，何況劣界。以無學者下上貪斷，於一切分已得安隱。了知是已，未離欲貪一分學者，於後無學心生願樂，見般涅槃寂靜功德。不復思惟一切相故，恒正思惟無相界故，於無相定勤修學故，

blocks.text: After a summary of the four verses, a new verse dialogue begins. Someone overwhelmed by desire says to the Buddha, "My mind is entirely ablaze." The Buddha prescribes four remedies. The treatise explains each with a question ("How does one…?") that Ru-Yi often leaves out; the omissions are marked.

Desired things come when their causes ripen. "If one performed no merit in a former life, however much effort one now applies, the desired object still fails to be realised." Master Cháng Bǎi: some grow richer the more they give; they planted the causes before. The first three verses, the treatise says, show the Buddha telling the deva that the monk could not unfold the teaching's full meaning; "only I can".

Venerable Miào Jìng: when craving is very heavy, it "comes and destroys one's pure mind". The cause is distorted perception: discarding the impure mark of an impure thing and grasping instead a seemingly lovely one. Master Cháng Bǎi: the body is impurity covered by thin skin; clinging to it as lovely makes the mind burn.

items: **Stay far from the alluring mark.** Venerable Miào Jìng: the main thing is to gather in the mind; when the mind is gathered, the senses follow.

**Impurity meditation, one-pointed.** One grasps the mark of a corpse, "turning livid, on through to bare bones", within concentration, and applies it after emerging to whatever appears attractive. Venerable Miào Jìng: "the body within" means one's own body and another's. Mindfulness binds the mind to the impure mark "as if tying it with a rope".
**See conditioned things as suffering and non-self.** Craving is the origin of suffering; "there exists no self… who, then, could be the one enjoying, and who the one enjoyed?"
**Sustained mindfulness of the body, cultivating revulsion,** for those whose craving is strong.

subs.head: What impurity meditation can and cannot do

blocks.text: In the untranslated prose that follows, the treatise notes that guarding the senses and reflecting on impurity, suffering, and non-self stop craving's present activity but not its latent tendency. Venerable Miào Jìng: impurity meditation can only subdue; Master Cháng Bǎi: the seeds of craving need non-self meditation to be cut.
This is a practical teaching for anyone overwhelmed by desire: first change what you attend to; then see its nature; then let insight remove the root.

quiz.q: Why does the treatise say desires "require their proper time"?
options: one must wait for a teacher's permission
they can be enjoyed only in old age
without past merit effort now fails; with merit only in this life, the object still does not come together now — it must wait
quiz.why: "If one performed no merit in a former life, then however much effort one now applies, one's desired object still fails to be realised. Or, if one performs merit only in this present life, the desired object still does not come together at this very time." Master Cháng Bǎi: some grow richer the more they give — they cultivated merit in past lives too.

quiz.q: What are the roles of the first three verses and the fourth? How was the deity's contempt removed?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the first three verses stop the deity's criticism of the monk, the fourth reveals the teaching's meaning; Miào Jìng: the first two show desire's suffering, the third — no self, no ranking — removes contempt and pride
quiz.why: "Here, the first three verses show the Blessed One speaking directly to the deity: the monk himself could not unfold the great meaning of the Tathāgata's teaching — only I can." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first three verses stop the deity's criticism of the monk, and the last reveals the teaching's most important meaning. Venerable Miào Jìng: the third verse shows there is no self, no pride, no distinction of equal, superior, or inferior — which is why it removes the contempt.

quiz.q: The deity says "crushed and obscured by craving-desire." How does Venerable Miào Jìng gloss 摧蔽?
options: heavy craving comes and destroys one's pure mind
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: when this craving is very heavy, it comes and destroys one's pure mind — that is "crushed and obscured." "My mind is entirely ablaze" means the mind is as if burned by a fierce fire.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define distorted perception?
options: regarding an impure object, discarding its impure mark and, through improper reflection, taking up a pure, alluring mark and its particulars
quiz.why: "Regarding an impure object, discarding its impure mark; through improper reflection, taking up instead a seemingly pure, alluring mark, along with its attractive particulars." Master Cháng Bǎi: distortedly clinging to a body — impurity covered by thin skin — as pure and lovely makes the mind burn as if on fire.

quiz.q: In cultivating impurity, what "mark belonging to wholesome concentration" does one first skilfully grasp?
options: the marks of a buddha image
a corpse turning livid, on through to bare bones or a scattered skeleton
quiz.why: "One first skilfully grasps the mark belonging to wholesome concentration — the mark of a corpse turning livid, and on through to bare bones, or a scattered skeleton." Master Cháng Bǎi: the mark of wholesome concentration refers to impurity meditation, which frees one from craving and brings concentration.

quiz.q: The treatise speaks of observing impurity in "the body within — one's own or another's." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say "the body within" covers?
options: one's own body and another's body are both called the body within
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "the body within" means both one's own body and another's body. Relying on the outer corpse breaks distorted perception; relying on the inner body is the general practice of impurity meditation.

quiz.q: Dwelling long in this practice severs fiercely intense craving. How deep is this severing, per the lectures?
options: impurity meditation only subdues present activity, not the seeds; those require continued non-self meditation
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: impurity meditation cannot sever the seeds; it can only subdue present activity. Master Cháng Bǎi: the seeds of craving still cannot be fully severed — one must continue with non-self meditation to sever them.
